fixes.explanation: Chewing the cud sounds like it should settle it, I know. But the camel, the rabbit and the rock badger only pass one test. Moses says they chew the cud, yet they don't have a divided hoof, so they are unclean for Israel (Deuteronomy 14:7). Both boxes have to be checked, friend. One out of two is a cookie with no chocolate chips, and nobody's calling that finished.

Right, and here's why. The camel, the rabbit and the rock badger chew the cud, but they don't have a divided hoof. Moses calls them unclean for Israel (Deuteronomy 14:7). One check passed and one missed means they stay off the list. It's like showing up to a job interview with a great resume and no pants. Half ready is not ready, friend.

Burning isn't what Moses asks for here. Look at the verb: Israel is to eat that tenth, along with the firstborn of the herds and flocks, in the presence of the LORD their God (Deuteronomy 14:23). The place is the one He will choose as a dwelling for His Name. So this one is a meal, friend. Bring an appetite.

The land never comes up in this reason. Moses says Israel is a people holy to the LORD their God, and that the LORD has chosen them out of all the peoples on the face of the earth (Deuteronomy 14:2). That's the whole reason on the table, friend. It's about who they belong to, not where they're standing.

False, and you nailed it, baker! Moses says, "All flying insects are unclean for you; they may not be eaten." (Deuteronomy 14:19) Not one bug with wings gets a pass. Mosquito, moth, whatever's buzzing around your porch light: all of it is off the menu. Honestly, I've never had to worry about that one in my bakery. My ovens stay bug free.
